content:
Aditya Rao: trying to lock go/no-go criteria for limited prod rollout of Optimize quality gates (hosted API, subset of routes). can folks drop final thresholds for: (1) pass rate, (2) flake rate, (3) eval runtime bounds. need something we can put in the launch checklist + communicate to leadership.

Talia Benson: +1, we need crisp numbers for the go/no-go doc + a clear owner per metric. also: are we gating both one-click apply + auto-apply for the limited rollout, or only one-click?

Paula Mendes: for limited rollout: enforce gates for both paths on the enrolled routes. auto-apply stays OFF by default for the first wave, but the enforcement plumbing is the same (apply boundary + rollout promotion). go/no-go should include “no bypass” checks.

Jonas Weber: proposed quality side criteria:
- Full gate tier: >= 95% pass rate on internal beta runs over trailing 7 days (excluding quarantined prompt sets).
- Smoke gate tier: >= 98% pass rate over trailing 7 days.
- Any single prompt set with > 10% failures (real failures, not flakes) is a stop-ship until triaged OR removed from the required set.
- Regression thresholding already encodes “no worse than baseline beyond delta + confidence,” so pass rate is mostly about harness stability + coverage.

Allison Grant: can we define pass rate as “% of gate runs that end in PASSED (after allowed reruns)”? otherwise we’ll debate partial failures forever. for metrics/alerts we were using:
- gate_run_outcome = passed|failed|overridden|canceled|errored|timed_out
- pass rate = passed / (passed + failed + errored + timed_out)
(ignoring canceled)

Jonas Weber: yep, that definition works. should also call out that “failed” includes quality regression and policy violations.

Sean Gallagher: SRE asks that go/no-go includes error/timeout ceilings + runtime ceilings. pass rate alone can hide timeouts.
- timeout rate <= 1% (timed_out / (passed+failed+timed_out+errored)) trailing 24h
- errored rate <= 0.5% trailing 24h
- queue wait p95 <= 10 min (otherwise gates block rollout pipelines too long)

Diego Ramos: for online signals: do we want a canary quality check as part of limited rollout criteria? even just “no spike in user-visible badness” guard.

Paula Mendes: for limited prod rollout go/no-go, we should keep online signal as “monitor-only” but require that dashboards exist and alerts are sane. we’re not blocking on online metrics yet (that’s v1). but we should require we can halt canary promotion if gates fail (already in rollout controller).

Marissa Cole: I want an explicit “no bypass” requirement. we had that near-miss last week where apply was possible via older internal endpoint. can we make go/no-go include validation that *all* config apply paths hit the gate enforcement? (UI, API, internal tooling)

Yara Haddad: +1. we have an allowlist of apply entrypoints now. we can add a checklist item:
- E2E test: config diff -> gate run -> apply blocked when failing
- E2E test: override granted -> apply allowed + audit event emitted
- negative test: direct apply attempt without gate_run_id returns 409

Kenji Nakamura: UX note: if we’re using pass rate >=95%, we should be ready for “why was this blocked?” customer confusion. go/no-go should include: Console copy finalized + links to artifacts visible + override request CTA present (even if override approvals are limited).

Aditya Rao: ok, let’s nail the flake definition + threshold. we’ve been using “rerun flips outcome” right?

Jonas Weber: current eval-harness flake scoring:
- flake = run where first attempt outcome != aggregated outcome after reruns (i.e., needed rerun to stabilize) OR where variance exceeds threshold.
- flake_rate = flake_runs / total_runs
proposal: flake_rate <= 3% trailing 7d for required suites.
if > 3% but <= 5%: still go if quarantining is working + no alert storms.
if > 5%: no-go.

Allison Grant: from alerting POV, agree: <=3% is manageable. above that we’ll get paging noise unless we dampen hard. also want:
- “quarantine action” must exist and be used (admin flag + reason code), otherwise teams just rerun until it passes.

Sean Gallagher: +1, and flake needs an operational path:
- oncall runbook published
- quarantine workflow + owner assignment
- alert policy: page only on sustained failure spike, not on single-suite flakes

i’d put those as go/no-go checklist items.

Talia Benson: summarizing so far (tell me if wrong):
QUALITY
- Full gates pass rate >= 95% trailing 7d (excluding quarantined)
- Smoke gates pass rate >= 98% trailing 7d (excluding quarantined)
FLAKINESS
- flake_rate <= 3% trailing 7d; 3-5% allowed only if suites are quarantined + no paging; >5% no-go
RELIABILITY
- timeout_rate <= 1% trailing 24h
- errored_rate <= 0.5% trailing 24h
- queue_wait p95 <= 10m
RUNTIME BOUNDS
- need numbers still

Paula Mendes: runtime bounds proposal (aligned with rollout coupling):
- smoke tier wall-clock p95 <= 8m, p99 <= 12m
- full tier wall-clock p95 <= 35m, p99 <= 60m
- hard cap: any single gate run > 75m counts as timed_out
and we should measure “time to first decision” separately (smoke gate result) since it unblocks most UI flows.

Jonas Weber: full tier p95 <= 35m is ok for limited rollout; later we should push it down. also note: runtime depends on GPU availability; queue_wait metric captures that.

Sean Gallagher: i’m fine with those bounds IF we have a lever to reduce concurrency / pause gate triggering when GPU pool is constrained. otherwise we’ll violate queue_wait p95.

Allison Grant: for go/no-go: require we have an emergency switch:
- disable new gate runs (but still enforce “no apply”)
- allow “manual apply with override” for urgent issues (RBAC restricted)

Marissa Cole: +1. limited prod rollout should ship with the “big red button” in case gates start timing out in eu-west (we saw it in staging once).

Diego Ramos: online canary note: even if monitor-only, can we add a lightweight check: “no >X% increase in customer-reported incidents attributed to Optimize apply blocks” for the first week? mostly a comms + support readiness thing.

Aditya Rao: yes, let’s add a support readiness criterion:
- #help macro + support doc
- if blocked, Console shows reason + artifact links
- escalation path for override (who approves)

Kenji Nakamura: approvals: for limited rollout, we said override approvers = oncall EM + PM on rotation? (per tightened policy). we should include that the UI shows expiration and reason required.

Paula Mendes: ok, so final go/no-go bullets i’ll write up:
1) Gate enforcement: zero known bypass paths; E2E tests green; apply without gate_run_id rejected
2) Pass rates: smoke >=98%, full >=95% trailing 7d (excluding quarantined)
3) Flake rate: <=3% trailing 7d; 3-5% only with quarantine + no alert storms; >5% no-go
4) Reliability: timeout <=1% trailing 24h; errored <=0.5%; queue_wait p95 <=10m
5) Runtime bounds: smoke p95<=8m/p99<=12m; full p95<=35m/p99<=60m; >75m => timed_out
6) Ops readiness: dashboards + alerts + runbook live; quarantine workflow usable; emergency switches documented
7) Support/UX: Console shows status + reasons + artifacts; override request/grant flow works; approver rotation set

Aditya Rao: looks good. Jonas/Sean/Allison can you :thumbsup: here if you’re ok with these being the hard go/no-go for the limited prod wave?

Jonas Weber: :thumbsup: from evals. caveat: pass rate math must exclude quarantined suites, and quarantine decisions must be logged.

Sean Gallagher: :thumbsup: SRE ok. please make queue_wait p95 a “hard” gate for go/no-go (it’s the early warning for region GPU scarcity).

Allison Grant: :thumbsup: ok. please also note in doc that “canceled” runs are excluded from denominator, and that alerts are based on (failed+errored+timed_out) not just failed.

Marissa Cole: :thumbsup: please make sure we have sign-off captured in the Linear launch ticket.

Talia Benson: i’ll paste this into the launch checklist and tag owners for daily reporting during rollout week. Aditya, send me the link once you put it in the PRD addendum.

Aditya Rao: will do. thanks all — i’ll update the go/no-go section and share in #eng-releases as well.
